Add an investigation report export feature to BugSleuth.

Requirements:
- Add a Flask endpoint that exports an existing investigation as a downloadable Markdown report.
- The report must include: investigation ID, project profile, evidence table with IDs, timeline, hypotheses, prosecutor argument, defense argument, judge verdict, limitations, and recommended next steps.
- Do not use external services or execute untrusted code. - Add a clearly labelled “Download Report” button to the completed investigation dashboard.
- Keep the visual design consistent with the existing interface.
- Add tests for the export endpoint.
- Update README.md with instructions for using this feature.

Please identify the files before changing them, then implement and explain the changes.

# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply. Three rules make this concrete:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.
Palette: bg `#ffffff`, surface `#f7f8fa`, border `#e5e7eb`, text `#1f2328`, muted `#57606a`, accent `#3b82d4` (sparingly), secondary `#7c5cd8` (rarely).

# Mode Switching

You can switch between different modes using the switch_mode tool. Each mode provides access to different capabilities and tools optimized for specific types of tasks.

Use `grep` to find code by content using regex patterns. Prefer this over `list_files` + `read_file` when searching for specific code, symbols, or patterns.
Use `read_file` only after grep tells you which file and lines to look at.

# Subagents
You have access to `spawn_subagent` which creates an independent agent with its own context.

**Default: do the work yourself.** Most tasks are faster and cheaper without a subagent.
Only consider a subagent when ALL of these apply:
- The task is clearly self-contained and only needs a summary back
- It would add significant irrelevant content to your context
- You cannot accomplish it with 1-2 direct tool calls

Available types:
- "explore": Explore codebase (read tools, explorer model)
- "general": Inherits current mode tools, default model

**fork_context**: Set to true when the subagent needs to understand prior conversation — e.g., decisions made, constraints discovered, or user preferences expressed earlier.
Leave false (default) when the description alone is sufficient context.

Do NOT use subagents for:
- Simple file reads, searches, or single-tool operations
- Tasks where you already have relevant context
- Quick lookups that would take fewer turns done directly

# create_chart — chart output
Use the `create_chart` tool when the user asks for a chart or data visualisation.

## How it works
Call the tool with:
- `type`: one of LineChart | BarChart | PieChart | ScatterChart | RadarChart | BoxplotChart
- `title`: short human-readable title for the chart tile
- `props`: a JSON string of chart-specific props

The props JSON must be valid for the chosen chart type. Do NOT wrap it in a spec fence.
Example for BarChart:
{"xAxisData":["Jan","Feb","Mar"],"series":[{"name":"Revenue","data":[4200,5800,3900]}],"title":"Monthly Revenue"}

Activate the `create-chart` skill before building props to get the full per-type prop schemas.

1 | # BugSleuth
2 | 
3 | BugSleuth is a local-first incident investigation web app for analyzing software failures with evidence instead of speculation. It accepts logs, source ZIP files, public GitHub URLs, and short observations, then builds a structured investigation report with project understanding, timeline analysis, and adversarial review.
4 | 
5 | ## Quick start
6 | 
7 | ### 1) Create a virtual environment
8 | 
9 | ```powershell
10 | cd "C:\path\to\P-v1"
11 | python -m venv .venv
12 | .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
13 | ```
14 | 
15 | ### 2) Install dependencies
16 | 
17 | ```powershell
18 | pip install -r requirements.txt
19 | ```
20 | 
21 | ### 3) Start the app
22 | 
23 | ```powershell
24 | python run.py
25 | ```
26 | 
27 | Then open:
28 | 
29 | ```text
30 | http://127.0.0.1:5000/
31 | ```
32 | 
33 | ## Project structure
34 | 
35 | ```text
36 | P-v1/
37 | ├── app.py                 # Flask application entry point
38 | ├── run.py                 # Simple startup script for normal users
39 | ├── requirements.txt       # Python dependencies
40 | ├── pytest.ini             # Pytest configuration
41 | ├── README.md              # Project guide
42 | ├── .gitignore             # Local-only ignore rules
43 | ├── docs/                  # Product notes and historical summaries
44 | │   ├── IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md
45 | │   └── V4_UPGRADE_SUMMARY.md
46 | ├── incident_data/         # Demo incident payloads and sample history
47 | ├── investigators/         # Investigation agents
48 | ├── models/                # Domain data models
49 | ├── services/              # Analysis and orchestration services
50 | ├── static/                # CSS and JavaScript assets
51 | ├── templates/             # HTML pages
52 | ├── tests/                 # Automated tests
53 | ├── tribunal/              # Prosecutor, Defense, and Judge modules
54 | ├── uploads/               # Temporary local upload storage
55 | ├── utils/                 # Shared helper utilities
56 | ├── verification/          # Proof and validation helpers
57 | ├── sample_app/            # Demo application used by sample evidence
58 | └── .venv/                 # Local virtual environment (not committed)
59 | ```
60 | 
61 | ## How the app works
62 | 
63 | 1. The user uploads evidence or provides a public GitHub repository URL.
64 | 2. The Flask app saves the submission in the local upload area.
65 | 3. Investigation services analyze logs, source code, and git history.
66 | 4. The tribunal modules evaluate the findings and return a conservative verdict.
67 | 5. The dashboard displays project profile, evidence, timeline, verdict, and recommended actions.
68 | 
69 | ## Safety and behavior
70 | 
71 | - uploaded files are stored locally in the `uploads/` folder
72 | - untrusted uploaded code is never executed
73 | - public GitHub repositories are supported
74 | - files are validated for size and unsafe zip paths
75 | 
76 | ## Run the tests
77 | 
78 | ```powershell
79 | pytest -q
80 | ```
81 | 
82 | ## Typical usage
83 | 
84 | 1. Open the app in a browser.
85 | 2. Click “Start New Investigation”.
86 | 3. Add logs, ZIP files, GitHub repository links, or a short observation.
87 | 4. Wait for analysis to complete.
88 | 5. Review the evidence, timeline, verdict, and recommendations.
89 | 
90 | ## Trust and verification
91 | 
92 | - Every directly cited item is assigned an `E-NNN` evidence ID and labelled as a fact.
93 | - Hypotheses and tribunal arguments cite those IDs and include a causal chain, counterargument, uncertainty, and the evidence that could change the verdict.
94 | - The dashboard distinguishes **Facts**, **Reasoning**, and **Verified Proof**.
95 | - RED → GREEN verification runs only for the bundled trusted demo, on a temporary copy. Uploaded and GitHub code is never executed.
96 | - The trust-layer API response is validated against a JSON Schema contract. See [incident package guidance](docs/INCIDENT_PACKAGES.md) for curated demo/regression cases.
97 | 
98 | ## Notes for normal users
99 | 
100 | This project is intentionally designed to run locally without external services or complex setup. The preferred startup command is:
101 | 
102 | ```powershell
103 | python run.py
104 | ```
105 | 
106 | This keeps the project easy to run and easy to understand for a non-technical user or a developer working quickly on a local machine.

"""
Report Service — generates a Markdown investigation report from a completed
investigation result.

The report is pure Python string formatting: no external libraries, no code
execution, no network calls.
"""

from datetime import datetime, timezone


def build_markdown_report(investigation_id: str, result: dict) -> str:
    """
    Build a downloadable Markdown report from a completed investigation result.

    Parameters
    ----------
    investigation_id : str
        The investigation identifier (e.g. INV-AABBCCDD or DEMO-INC-2026-001).
    result : dict
        The dict returned by run_investigation().

    Returns
    -------
    str
        A UTF-8 Markdown document suitable for writing to a .md file.
    """
    lines: list[str] = []

    def h1(text: str) -> None:
        lines.extend([f"# {text}", ""])

    def h2(text: str) -> None:
        lines.extend([f"## {text}", ""])

    def h3(text: str) -> None:
        lines.extend([f"### {text}", ""])

    def para(text: str) -> None:
        lines.extend([str(text), ""])

    def rule() -> None:
        lines.extend(["---", ""])

    # ── Title ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    h1("BugSleuth Investigation Report")
    generated_at = datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC")
    para(f"**Investigation ID:** `{investigation_id}`  ")
    para(f"**Generated:** {generated_at}  ")
    para(f"**Mode:** {result.get('mode', 'user')}  ")
    rule()

    # ── 1. Project Profile ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
    h2("1. Project Profile")
    incident = result.get("incident") or {}
    rows = [
        ("Service", incident.get("service", "—")),
        ("Title", incident.get("title", "—")),
        ("Severity", incident.get("severity", "—")),
        ("Deployment version", incident.get("deployment_version", "—")),
        ("Incident start", incident.get("incident_start", "—")),
        ("User impact", incident.get("user_impact", "—")),
        ("Error summary", incident.get("error_summary", "—")),
    ]
    lines.append("| Field | Value |")
    lines.append("| ----- | ----- |")
    for label, value in rows:
        lines.append(f"| {_md_cell(label)} | {_md_cell(str(value))} |")
    lines.append("")

    description = incident.get("description", "")
    if description and description not in (incident.get("error_summary", ""), "—"):
        para(f"**Description:** {description}")

    rule()

    # ── 2. Evidence Table ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    h2("2. Evidence Table")
    trust_layer = result.get("trust_layer") or {}
    facts = trust_layer.get("facts") or []
    if facts:
        lines.append("| ID | Source | Kind | Direct | Content |")
        lines.append("| -- | ------ | ---- | ------ | ------- |")
        for fact in facts:
            fid     = _md_cell(fact.get("id", "—"))
            source  = _md_cell(fact.get("source", "—"))
            kind    = _md_cell(fact.get("kind", "—"))
            direct  = "Yes" if fact.get("direct") else "No"
            content = _md_cell(fact.get("content", "—"))
            lines.append(f"| {fid} | {source} | {kind} | {direct} | {content} |")
        lines.append("")
    else:
        para("*No catalogued evidence facts were recorded for this investigation.*")

    rule()

    # ── 3. Investigation Timeline ────────────────────────────────────────────
    h2("3. Investigation Timeline")
    timeline = result.get("timeline") or []
    if timeline:
        lines.append("| Step | Agent | Status | Findings |")
        lines.append("| ---- | ----- | ------ | -------- |")
        for i, step in enumerate(timeline, 1):
            agent    = _md_cell(step.get("agent", "—"))
            status   = _md_cell(step.get("status", "—"))
            findings = step.get("findings_count")
            count    = str(findings) if findings is not None else "—"
            lines.append(f"| {i} | {agent} | {status} | {count} |")
        lines.append("")
    else:
        para("*No timeline data available.*")

    rule()

    # ── 4. Hypotheses ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    h2("4. Leading Hypothesis")
    hypothesis = result.get("hypothesis", "")
    if hypothesis:
        para(f"> {hypothesis}")
    else:
        para("*No hypothesis was formed.*")

    supporting_ids = (trust_layer.get("hypothesis") or {}).get("evidence_ids") or []
    if supporting_ids:
        para(f"**Supporting evidence IDs:** {', '.join(supporting_ids)}")

    rule()

    # ── 5. Prosecutor Argument ───────────────────────────────────────────────
    tribunal = result.get("tribunal") or {}
    prosecution = tribunal.get("prosecutor") or {}

    h2("5. Prosecutor Argument")
    para(f"**Position:** {prosecution.get('position', '—')}")
    para(prosecution.get("argument", "*No argument recorded.*"))

    evidence_ids = prosecution.get("evidence_ids") or []
    if evidence_ids:
        para(f"**Evidence cited:** {', '.join(evidence_ids)}")

    causal_chain = prosecution.get("causal_chain") or []
    if causal_chain:
        h3("Causal Chain")
        for step in causal_chain:
            label   = step.get("label", "?")
            desc    = step.get("description", "")
            eid     = step.get("evidence_id", "")
            eid_str = f" `{eid}`" if eid else ""
            lines.append(f"- **[{label.upper()}]**{eid_str} {desc}")
        lines.append("")

    rule()

    # ── 6. Defense Argument ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
    defense = tribunal.get("defense") or {}

    h2("6. Defense Argument")
    para(defense.get("argument", "*No argument recorded.*"))

    alternatives = defense.get("alternatives") or []
    if alternatives:
        h3("Alternative Explanations")
        for alt in alternatives:
            lines.append(f"- {alt}")
        lines.append("")

    missing = defense.get("missing_evidence") or []
    if missing:
        h3("Missing Evidence Flagged by Defense")
        for item in missing:
            lines.append(f"- {item}")
        lines.append("")

    rule()

    # ── 7. Judge Verdict ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    judge = tribunal.get("judge") or {}

    h2("7. Judge Verdict")
    verdict_value = judge.get("verdict", "UNKNOWN")
    para(f"**Verdict:** `{verdict_value}`")
    para(f"**Confidence:** {judge.get('confidence_level', '—')} ({int((judge.get('confidence') or 0) * 100)}%)")
    para(f"**Reason:** {judge.get('reason', '—')}")

    best = judge.get("best_current_assessment", "")
    if best:
